primaryProduct.audience: Small nonprofits managing recurring donors and nonprofit purchases
primaryProduct.pitch: An after-hours donor line completes eligible gift changes and hardship relief, preserves the nonprofit's funding through an authorized sponsor, and produces evidence of what actually happened. A supply desk extends the same approval and recovery system to buying volunteer merchandise.
primaryProduct.donorJourney: The caller unlocks a configured demonstration donor with a PIN, asks for a supported gift action, reviews exact terms, gives fresh explicit consent, and receives a signed receipt only after authoritative provider confirmation. Eligible Covered Month hardship relief confirms sponsor capture before refunding the donor while leaving the recurring gift active. An unrecognized charge has a different review policy; arbitrary disputes are not automatically resolved.
primaryProduct.supplyJourney: Type a buying goal or enter limits manually. Claude drafts editable quantity, USD budget, goods, exact delivery date/time and split permission, or asks for missing information. Drafting grants no quote or payment authority. Find a plan explicitly contacts supplier MCP endpoints. Claude proposes bounded counteroffers, suppliers return binding terms, code validates and selects complete allocations, Jev advises, and the buyer approves one exact plan plus each separate PayPal sandbox order. Unknown settlement blocks a later supplier and a replacement purchase until checked safely.
primaryProduct.coherence: The donor line leads the landing page and guided demo; purchasing is presented as another task for the same nonprofit. These remain two substantial workflows, rather than a single narrow donor-relief feature.

demonstratedEngineering: Anthropic Sonnet 5.5 is the main agent. Jev 1.14.0 performs advisory review and a constrained quick route. Neither model interprets pending consent, authorizes payment, changes a registered payee, or confirms settlement.

Jev quick routing needs confidence and selected probability at least 0.99, agreement with the rules router, and membership in a fixed read-only allowlist. Other reasoning uses Claude; mutation disagreement asks again. Pending consent is processed by deterministic code with zero model calls.

Goal interpretation has a strict bounded tool contract, server-provided time/timezone, explicit delivery date AND time, USD-only limits and exposed default assumptions. Model omissions of default-USD disclosure are corrected by code. It never creates a supplier session or payment; manual entry remains available.

Three project-controlled HTTP/MCP supplier servers require bearer authorization and initialization, enforce registered merchants, immutable quote identities, expiry, merchandise, quantities, stock and commercial terms. The supplier lab is hosted privately inside the existing service and persists issued quotes in Neon.

A grouped dynamic program considers valid initial, deterministic-counteroffer and model-counteroffer alternatives with at most one quote per supplier. It includes setup, shipping, tax, exact quantities, delivery and budget. The final selected cost cannot exceed a feasible deterministic baseline. Baseline wins ties. The model may use up to two negotiations per supplier, with no hidden retry.

The displayed bounded negotiation trace distinguishes initial offers, baseline offers, exact model counteroffer and rationale, supplier responses, stable rejection codes, selected allocation and price-guard comparisons. Approved traces and reviewer evidence persist with the exact plan; unapproved quote sessions remain in memory.

Jev review shows confidence and stable reason codes alongside nine deterministic constraint checks. Low confidence is explicitly distinct from a failed constraint. Review is advisory and never grants payment authority.

Neon PostgreSQL stores approved terms, capability hashes, one-attempt claims, provider identities, donor calls/actions and verified webhooks. Financial attempts commit before dispatch. Startup checks required schemas without migrations or an in-memory fallback. Restricted runtime privileges and hosted contention/immutability checks were exercised.

Recovery uses authoritative reads of the same provider identity. It does not replay an uncertain write or automatically replace/refund a partial order. Some outcomes without a returned provider identity remain unknown; this is explicitly blocked rather than called successful.

PayPal webhook signatures are checked and durably recorded before HTTP200. Verified duplicates do not duplicate ledger effects. Stable Ed25519 receipts verify after local restart and hosted redeployment. A receipt proves the app's signature and unchanged contents, not PayPal's signature or live settlement.

Explicit provider API keys and fixed API hosts only: no Claude chat session, subscription OAuth, CLI credential chain or automatic funding fallback. Shared durable reservations and a latched stop block both AI providers on local exhaustion, billing/authentication failure or unverifiable usage. Provider account balances are not available through these keys; exact account-zero polling is not claimed.

actualSandboxFinancialAcceptance.purchase: A composed Claude/Jev/MCP request for 100 shirts within $800 completed two PayPal sandbox captures: 60 shirts for $396.50 and 40 for $279.75, total $676.25. Fresh provider reads and Neon matched, with one create and one capture attempt per leg. App and private supplier lab restarted between the two legs; the original browser session recovered the partial order and completed the second leg. This is historical acceptance before the new price guard, so the recording correctly retains $676.25 rather than rewriting it as the newer $674.15 plan.
actualSandboxFinancialAcceptance.donor: The configured test subscription was paused and resumed with separate consent and authoritative reads. A $25 sponsor capture and $25 donor refund both completed; the recurring gift stayed ACTIVE. A $1.36 capture fee was recorded: equal gross amounts are not fee-free coverage. A separate disposable test subscription was explicitly cancelled with one confirmed attempt while the main subscription stayed active.
actualSandboxFinancialAcceptance.invoiceAndWebhook: The application created and sent a $50 sandbox invoice after consent; the buyer paid it through PayPal's authenticated sandbox wallet. Fresh API reads showed PAID with a successful sale. The genuine paid webhook was signature-verified and stored before acknowledgment; a genuine redelivery left one journal row, one verified ledger row and one payment. The accepted invoice and signed receipt survived process replacement. The first invoice draft had been refused403 for missing app permission; it created no invoice. Permission was corrected before a fresh proposal and consent.
actualSandboxFinancialAcceptance.externality: All supplier endpoints are controlled by the project and use one owned sandbox merchant. This is actual PayPal sandbox processing, not independent supplier fulfillment, inventory verification or real-money acceptance.

designAndPresentationEvidence.observed: Consistent restrained warm off-white typography-led interface, Geist/Instrument Serif, clear step structure, keyboard labels/status regions, distinct exact approval controls. Actual 390px and768px browser checks showed no horizontal overflow; no console errors in observed flows. The assessor receives this text description, not screenshots, and cannot independently certify visual polish or accessibility compliance.
designAndPresentationEvidence.demo: An anonymous four-chapter /demo leads with donor relief, then nonprofit purchasing, restart recovery and signed proof. It includes a73-second1280x720 narrated historical evidence walkthrough with captions, clear sandbox/lab labels, payment fee caveat and live-disabled disclosure. Anonymous original receipt verification passed; an edited amount was rejected. Video is a narrated summary of accepted records, not a continuous new live microphone/checkout session or target-user study.
designAndPresentationEvidence.documentation: Versioned acceptance evidence, both negative and corrective evaluations, a concise judge demo script, and an explicit real-money readiness report are included. Old scores have been deliberately omitted from this packet to avoid numerical anchoring.

impactAndRemainingGaps.marketContext: The2026M+R nonprofit benchmark reports monthly giving was27% of online giving in2025; small organizations' cohort was22%. This is secondary context for the problem, not measured benefit of this app. No participant in that study tested Pledge Line. Sources checked Nov5: https://mrbenchmarks.com/ and https://mrbenchmarks.com/fundraising/.
impactAndRemainingGaps.validation: No outside nonprofit/donor usability study, sponsor willingness, retention uplift, time saved, willingness to pay or adoption has been observed. The user asked to complete software before an optional usability session. No invented testimonials or tasks replace that missing evidence. Newly observed real microphone usage is not established in this completion pass.
impactAndRemainingGaps.aiDifferentiation: The protection, execution and recovery mechanisms work, but neither frozen comparison shows the model outperforming its strong deterministic baseline. Claude interpretation is a bounded optional input method with review, not demonstrated economic advantage or broad semantic reliability.
impactAndRemainingGaps.realMoney: Production is intentionally blocked. Required next: named legal merchant ownership and verified account; donor-specific authentication and ownership instead of the shared demo PIN; actual sponsor mandate; independent supplier authority and applicable PayPal platform/seller onboarding; separate reviewed live adapter/credentials/database namespace; monitoring, incident ownership and tested backup restoration; separately authorized bounded live settlement/refund acceptance. Neon durability alone supplies none of those permissions.
impactAndRemainingGaps.operations: One existing free Render service and Neon database. Startup/runtime restrictions, durability, duplicate handling and bounded recovery are tested, but this is not an availability SLA, audited production service or demonstrated independent fulfillment operation.
impactAndRemainingGaps.builder: The project contains demonstrated implementation and integration work, sandbox operational access and detailed evidence. No nonprofit partner, sponsor relationship, independent supplier access or founder-specific domain advantage is documented.
impactAndRemainingGaps.competition: The user proposed Best Use of Agentic Commerce and Best Overall categories. Current official event eligibility, deadlines, category rules and submission compliance were not independently established.
